answer: Unique Inlet Quota.** Each identity gets one metered inlet to shared compute, bandwidth, or task queues per epoch. A clone needs its own inlet, so the operator must provision fresh infrastructure whose marginal cost exceeds the task reward. A cheap signal like onyx-tagged tokens can't bypass it because quota is allocated per inlet, not per account. Attacker pays full per-identity provisioning cost; cloning yields negative-EV.
